procedure_file: extraction_procedure_social_addendum_v1.3_social science Classes 6-10 on top of procedure v2.md

count_gate.note: printed difficulty table 15/28/7=50 DISAGREES with per-question tags 10/35/5 (source defect, tags win v2 §6; register difficulty-table-vs-tags); flagged counts answer-level flags; all carry the structural marks flag (addendum §4.5).

method_notes: CHAPTER ANSWER-KEY UNRELIABLE (control rev-4 finding): ~13/32 section-A MCQ letter-keys + vsa q41 are factually wrong in the SOURCE grid (pdf176); printed keys asserted verbatim + per-question 'key text does not address question' review flags; flagged for review-method-v1.3.
ch4 single numbering 1-50; sections A mcq(1-32) B vsa(33-41) C sa(42-46) D sa(47-48) E la(49-50) = s1-s5.
MCQ keys are LETTER-ONLY (grid '1.D 2.D...'); passed as 'X)' so the builder resolves by printed letter.

SECTION-LEVEL MARKS printed: C '(2 marks)', D '(3 marks)', E '(4 marks)' -> recorded in marks flag text; marks left null (assigning section-sourced marks is a procedure change, not extraction's — surfaced for a marks ruling like the section-header-difficulty case).
all questions carry per-question difficulty tags (A q1-32 Average; B Easy; C mixed; D/E Difficult) -> no section-header difficulty needed.
C/D/E keys are sub-headed bullet lists (some a-e/a-k lettered) -> SUB; heading excluded from solution_steps. marks not printed per question (addendum §4.5) beyond the section notes.

The British fortified Fort William in Calcutta without the permission of Siraj-ud-Daula.

Siraj-ud-Daula seized British factories and trading posts.

questions.text: Explain the consequences of the Battle of Plassey, which laid a solid foundation for the establishment of the British Empire in India
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the consequences of the Battle of Plassey, which laid a solid foundation for the establishment of the British Empire in India (Difficult )

answer.value:
Consequences of the Battle of Plassey:
a. Mir Jafar became the Nawab: Mir Jafar was installed as the Nawab of Bengal.
b. British puppet: Mir Jafar became a puppet ruler under British control.
c. Grant of zamindari rights: The British East India Company gained zamindari rights over the 24 Parganas district.
d. Led to the Battle of Buxar: The Battle of Plassey ultimately led to the Battle of Buxar.
e. British traders became rulers: The British, who were initially traders, began to administer the region.
f. Establishment of British Empire: The Battle of Plassey marked the beginning of the establishment of the British Empire in India.

questions.text: Discuss the role of the 'Carnatic Wars' in the rise of the British in India
questions.text_as_printed: Discuss the role of the 'Carnatic Wars' in the rise of the British in India (Difficult )

answer.value:
The Carnatic Wars and the Rise of the British in India:
a. The Carnatic region was a province of the Mughal Empire and a rich hinterland of the Coromandel Coast.
b. The region's wealth and strategic location made it a prized target for European powers.
c. The rivalry between the French and British for trade control in India led to the Carnatic Wars.
d. The Carnatic Wars were a series of three conflicts between the British and French.
e. The control of this prosperous region and its trade was the primary cause of the wars.
f. Therefore, the Carnatic region played a crucial role in the Carnatic Wars.

questions.text: Give the reason why historians call the 18th century the 'period of Maratha supremacy'.
questions.text_as_printed: Give the reason why historians call the 18th century the 'period of Maratha supremacy'. (Difficult )

answer.value:
The 18th Century: The Era of Maratha Supremacy:
a. The Marathas rose to prominence in the 18th century, during the decline of the Mughal Empire.
b. Shivaji was the founder of the Maratha kingdom.
c. Shivaji established a strong and independent kingdom despite the powerful Mughal and Bahmani empires.
d. Shivaji appointed eight ministers, known as the Ashta Pradhan, to assist him in governance.
e. The Peshwa was the Prime Minister of the Maratha kingdom.
f. Under the leadership of the Peshwas, the Marathas emerged as a major political and military power in India.
g. Notable Peshwas include Balaji Vishwanath, Baji Rao I, and Balaji Baji Rao.
h. The period from approximately 1713 to 1818 was the era of Maratha dominance.
i. Seven Peshwas ruled India during this period.
j. The Marathas resisted the British and Mughals, working towards establishing a Hindu empire in India.
k. Therefore, the 18th century is often referred to as the era of Maratha supremacy.
